issues.description: Class 'Animal' constructor and attributes are inconsistent between the problem statement (UML + task text) and the provided code. The UML in problem_statement.md declares Animal with two attributes (name: String and age: int) and a constructor signature 'Animal(String, int)'. The solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) declares only a single 'name' attribute and a single-argument constructor 'Animal(String)'. The template Main.java also instantiates subclasses using single-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). This contradiction (expected two-parameter constructor vs. actual one-parameter constructor and missing 'age' attribute) will confuse students about which constructor and attributes they must implement and can lead to mismatches when students follow the UML or the template examples.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the Animal API consistent across all artifacts. Two reasonable fixes (choose one based on intended learning goals):

Option A (remove age): Update problem_statement.md (UML and task text) to remove the 'age: int' attribute and change the UML constructor to 'Animal(String)'. This aligns the specification with the template and solution. Ensure all textual references to Animal constructor/age are updated.

Option B (add age): Update the template and solution code to include the 'age' attribute and change the constructor to 'Animal(String, int)'. Add getter/setter for age, update all subclass constructors (Seal, Pig, Goat) to call super(name, age), and update Main.java example instantiations to pass an age value. Also update tests and any example usages accordingly.

Apply the chosen option consistently to problem_statement.md, the template repository, and the solution repository so students and automated tests see the same constructor signature and attributes.
